title: cost bench & telemetry advisor: automated microbenchmarks to suggest batching/quant defaults
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: Customers consistently ask for safe, tenant-specific defaults for batching, cache prefill, and quantization that balance latency SLOs and unit cost. Manual profiling is slow and error-prone. This PR introduces a lightweight automated bench/telemetry pipeline (cost-bench) that runs microbenchmarks against representative request samples and uses observed token-latency/cost curves plus live telemetry to recommend conservative defaults and quantization presets for tenants and models.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds a CLI command (cmd/costbench) that runs deterministic microbenchmarks against a selected model variant and tenant config, emitting a compact report and a candidate "defaults.json" for that tenant.
- Implements an on-device scoring function in internal/econ/benchscore.go that converts observed per-token latency + memory footprint into a unit-econ score and risk band (safe / experimental / avoid).
- Adds telemetry exporter hooks (telemetry/exporters/costbench) to upload sanitized microbenchmark summaries into the existing econ telemetry stream for later aggregation. Export includes model id, sequence profile, batch size tried, quant profile, p50/p95 per-token latency, and score. No customer PII is included.
- Adds an advisor service (internal/econ/advisor.go) that consumes bench results + historical telemetry to pick a recommended batch size, cache presize (kv-prefetch), and quant preset (int8 / fp16 / q4_* profiles) with a confidence score and suggested rollout plan.
- Adds integration tests and a smoke test harness to perf-canary that validates recommendations don't regress p95 beyond tenant-configured SLOs.
- Adds docs: docs/cost-bench.md with usage examples and a section on safeguards and how to interpret the produced defaults.json.

Design notes:
- The bench runner is conservative by default: it starts at the tenant's current baseline and only proposes smaller batch sizes or more aggressive quant when unit-econ improves with <5% p95 latency increase (configurable).
- Recommendations are accompanied by a rollout recipe: canary percent, safety timeout, and an automatic rollback trigger if live p95 increases >2x from bench prediction.
- Benchmarks are sampled from tenant traffic or synthetic traces; the CLI supports a --synthetic flag for reproducible experiments.

Checklist (manual steps & automated checks):
- [x] Implement bench runner CLI and core scoring algorithm
- [x] Wire telemetry exporter with minimal, sanitized payloads
- [x] Implement advisor scoring and rollout recipe generation
- [x] Add unit and integration tests covering edge cases (cold vs warm KV cache, short vs long sequences)
- [x] Add docs + example defaults.json and suggested canary config
- [x] Security review for telemetry payloads (no PII, KMS keys unchanged)
- [x] Perf smoke test in perf-canary pipeline

High-level commits: ["init cost-bench CLI and runner", "bench scoring function + advisor prototype", "telemetry exporter + proto registration", "docs + examples", "tests and perf-canary integration", "fix: race in bench runner teardown"].

ci_summary: All CI checks passed on second run. One flaky test (TestBenchRunner/teardown) failed on first run and was retried; subsequent run passed. Checks: build (pass), unit (pass), integration (pass), lint (pass), perf-smoke (pass).
merge_notes: Squashed and merged after addressing telemetry schema and adding rollout unit test. Deployed advisor as feature-flag behind econ.advisor.enabled=false by default.
release_notes: Added 'cost-bench' CLI and advisor that produce tenant-specific batching, cache, and quant defaults based on microbenchmarks and telemetry. Feature gated behind econ.advisor.enabled; opt-in recommended for controlled canaries.
sr_notes: Support: If customers report unexpected latency after applying recommendations, revert using the produced rollout recipe or set econ.advisor.enabled=false. Attach cost-bench report when opening tickets.
testing_notes: Perf-canary uses synthetic traces to validate recommendation safety. Manual steps: run `redwood cost-bench run --tenant <id> --model <id> --out ./defaults.json` then review defaults.json before applying. See docs/cost-bench.md for full guidance.
